accent.comment: The one colour that means HERE, and the one that means ACT: the fill of the primary action, the selected row, the filter that is on, the count of what waits on the reader, and the hue the focus ring is drawn in. A fill and a mark, never text. Per palette: this marketing root and the dark palette take the approved #7c56ff, and light repaints it #6b45f0. On this one white clears 4.53:1, so it is as light as the accent can be while the label of a primary button still clears the text floor.

accentHover.comment: A step DARKER, never brighter: the least move along lightness, keeping hue and chroma, that a reader can see (dE 3.08), and a move away from the white label, which it takes from 4.53:1 to 5.18:1. The approved hover brightened the fill instead (brightness(1.08), #865dff) and measured 4.18:1, under the text floor at the moment the button is about to be pressed.

accentActive.comment: One step further on the same line, dE 3.05 past the hover. White clears 5.92:1.

accentInk.comment: The accent as TEXT, the approved step, and 5.90:1 at its tightest, on a pressed row inside a raised surface. The fill step is never text and this step is never a background; the split is what the palette suite measures. Light repaints it to a dark violet.

accentSoft.comment: Translucent accent fill behind a selected row: this palette's accent at the approved 0.16. The alpha is per palette, because a selected row has to separate from its ground by at least as much as a plain hover overlay does, and by dE 3 from the overlay itself, and one alpha cannot do both on a dark ground and a light one. Its companions are derived from the accent by the build: accentRgb, the accent as an r, g, b triple for a translucent tint of a stylesheet's own (rgba(var(--color-brand-accent-rgb), 0.12)), and accentSoftStrong, the accent at 0.32, the border paired with this fill.

accentDeep.comment: Deep purple. Distinct from the accent; used as a gradient stop and rarely on its own.

highlight.comment: Hot pink highlight. The first stop of the brand gradient; use sparingly on its own.

slate.comment: Muted blue-grey for low-emphasis informational fills (toast progress drains, hover halos, info notification tints).

mark.comment: The logo's own colour, and the default of the brand figure. It belongs to the mark rather than to the interface, so it is the same in every palette and is never spent on a control.

gradient.comment: Brand gradient. The one 4-stop definition every gradient surface uses, so marketing and product surfaces match.

frame.comment: The FRAME, the lowest of the four rungs: the application ground under the rail and around the floating sheet, and what the document baseline paints the body with. The marketing palette is one black ground, so here it is the page's own black; each theme lifts its sheet off it.

background.comment: The SHEET: the ground page content sits on, floating inside the frame. It keeps the name every component already reads for 'the ground content sits on', the focus ring's inner ring and a mask drawn in the page's colour among them.

subtle.comment: The CARD: a card, a popover, a dialog body. Near-flat on the sheet on purpose, because a card is found by its hairline, --color-border-default, which the palette suite holds to dE 3 on both sides of it.

elevated.comment: RAISED: a chip, a segmented well, a key cap, a meter track, a lifted row. It has no border of its own, so its fill is held dE 3 off the card.

hover.comment: The overlay a hovered row carries. A row shows this OR the selected tint, never both: they are the same property on the same element, so the tinted row keeps its tint and the palette suite measures no hover-over-selected composite.

inset.comment: A well: a code block, an empty state, a panel sunk into its card.

glass.comment: Frosted chrome, paired with --blur-sm. Glass carries chrome; anything carrying words sits on an opaque surface. The alpha is 0.90 because that is what keeps the tertiary text step over 4.5:1 (4.78:1 here) with the inverse ground behind it, the far end of the palette from the glass and so the worst backdrop a panned canvas can put there.

scrim.comment: A ground that DARKENS what is behind it: a media viewer, an upload target, the rail's own overlay on a phone. It is not what a dialog sits on; see veil.

veil.comment: The ground a dialog, a sheet and the command palette sit on. It is THE ROOT'S OWN FRAME at 0.65, which is this root's black here and a theme's own frame there, so the application is faded back into its own ground rather than darkened out of the way: an operator keeps their place while a surface is open. Held to the ground it belongs to, and not to one theme's value: a veil that is a different colour from what it covers is a wash over it rather than the application seen through less of itself. The alpha is what holds the page's own primary text inside a band, below the 3:1 mark floor so nothing behind competes with the surface and above 1.5:1 so the page is still there. The palette suite measures both ends.

inverse.comment: The ground that inverts the palette, carrying --color-text-inverse.

primary.comment: Slightly off-white to reduce eye strain on dark surfaces.

tertiary.comment: A fact, so it clears 4.5:1 on every surface it can land on, including a pressed row inside a raised surface. #8c99ad measured 4.17:1 there.

muted.comment: DECORATION ONLY: a hairline glyph, a disabled affordance, a border. Measured BETWEEN 2.8:1 and 4.5:1 on the panel, because a step that crept up to the fact floor would invite itself into a table cell, which is the whole reason it has a separate name.

onAccent.comment: The label on an accent fill, and on the danger fill. White in every palette: a primary button whose label changed colour with the theme would read as two different buttons.

strong.comment: The heavier resting border, at the plain border's hover weight. It used to hold the same value as --color-border-default in both palettes, so the pair was a copy of the plain pair rather than a third step.

strongHover.comment: One step past strong, so the strong pair is a real pair.

control.comment: The boundary of an input, a checkbox or a switch. It clears 3:1 on every surface a control can sit on, the overlay composites included: a checkbox inside a hovered row in a dialog body is the case the opaque surfaces alone do not catch.

focus.comment: The focus indicator, drawn as an OUTLINE at 2px and offset 2px. Forced-colors mode drops every box-shadow and keeps outlines, so a ring drawn as a shadow alone disappears for exactly the readers who need one. It is the ACCENT, lightened dE 1.06 along lightness, the dark palette's value, which clears this root too (3.01:1): #7c56ff itself measured 2.89:1 on a pressed row inside a raised surface, under the 3:1 a ring has to clear, and the accent cannot make that move for it, because any lighter takes the white label of a primary button under the text floor.

success.comment: DONE: work that finished. The four states are what a piece of work is doing, and their meanings never move: info is working, warning needs a person, danger is stopped, success is done. The names stay generic because a badge, a callout and a toast mean the same four things. Every value here is the dark palette's, the approved design's moved the least the floors allow; tokens/themes/dark.json says what moved each.

warning.comment: NEEDS A PERSON: work that is waiting on somebody.

danger.comment: STOPPED: work that failed or was halted, and the fill of a destructive action. The one hue that means the same thing everywhere in a product, so every chart series is held away from it.

dangerHover.comment: The destructive action under the pointer: a visible step darker, away from its white label.

onboarding.comment: The agent phases: onboarding, execute, review. Three, and the only categorical identity outside a chart. Every pair stays dE 10 apart under normal, protan and deutan vision, and clears the status family and the accent under all three.

execute.comment: The dark palette's value, moved with it: tokens/themes/dark.json says why.

1.comment: Four series in a fixed order, blue, orange, aqua and yellow, plus a neutral residual, and legal ONLY inside a figure that names them: a legend for two series or more, the label for one. Neighbours are what a legend reader distinguishes, so that is what is measured: dE 9 apart under every vision and 15 under normal vision. Series 1 is deliberately NOT the accent: a series painted in the selection colour claims to be the selection. The values are the dark palette's.

other.comment: The residual bucket. Exempt from the separation rules on purpose: a residual that competed with a real series would be claiming to be one.

0.comment: The ten seeded avatar grounds, chosen by a stable hash when a consumer passes a colour seed. Each clears 4.5:1 under white initials; five of them were darkened along OKLab lightness to get there, keeping their hue and chroma.

purple.comment: Six hues a node of a chart is tinted with, chosen per entity and NOT a series: two nodes sharing one is no statement, so nothing here is measured for separability and no legend is owed. Each hue derives a fill, a border and a halo at fixed alphas, and carries an ink step for the name drawn on that fill, because the tinted card is the only ground that name is read on. The dark values are the muted set the console chart was drawn with, tuned to sit beside the accent rather than beside neon; light repaints every one, since a tint tuned for black is a wash on white.

purpleInk.comment: The name drawn on the purple fill. It clears 7:1 there, as every ink step here does.

scrollbar.comment: Scrollbars belong to the palette. A bright system gutter down the side of a dark page is the most visible way an application admits it is a web page.
